record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: Can Rumanov’s explicit Painlevé-II-based description of the Tracy–Widom distribution for β=6 be made fully rigorous, and can the same program be carried out rigorously for all even β>0?

evidence.quote: It is of great interest to complete Rumanov’s analysis rigorously, not only for β = 6, but for all even β > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. For β > 0, the Tracy–Widom_β distribution F_β is the limiting distribution of the appropriately rescaled largest eigenvalue of the Gaussian β-ensemble. It is known that F_1, F_2, F_4 admit explicit representations in terms of the Hastings–McLeod solution q(x) of the second Painlevé equation q''(x) = x q(x) + 2 q(x)^3, characterized by the asymptotic q(x) ~ Ai(x) as x → +∞. For general β, Bloemendal and Virág showed that F_β(x) = lim_{y→+∞} f(x,y) for a function f satisfying a linear PDE (the Bloemendal–Virág equation) with prescribed boundary conditions.

A formal construction (due to Rumanov, for β = 6) produces a Lax-pair / gauge transformation of the standard Painlevé-II Lax pair that yields an explicit representation of F_6(x) in terms of the Hastings–McLeod Painlevé-II transcendent q(x) together with an auxiliary function w(x) satisfying a certain second-order nonlinear ODE whose coefficients involve q. An analogous formal scheme is expected for every even integer β.

Problem. 
(a) Establish rigorously the explicit Painlevé-II–based representation of the Tracy–Widom distribution F_6: in particular, prove the integrability/solvability of the auxiliary ODE arising in the construction, justify the boundary conditions linking the constructed solution to F_6 via the Bloemendal–Virág equation, and thereby derive rigorous large-x asymptotics for F_6 from this representation.
(b) Extend the construction rigorously to all even integers β > 0: for each such β, produce an explicit description of F_β in terms of the Painlevé-II transcendent and a finite system of auxiliary ODEs, and prove that this description correctly represents the Tracy–Widom_β distribution.
artifact.status_search_result: For β = 6, partial rigorous progress exists: Its and collaborators reinterpreted Rumanov's Lax pair as a gauge transformation of the standard Painlevé-II Lax pair and proved that the underlying Painlevé function is the Hastings–McLeod transcendent, obtaining a second-order ODE for the logarithmic derivative of F_6. However, the integrability of the auxiliary ODE in Rumanov's representation — needed for full rigor and asymptotic analysis — is reported as still open, and the analogous program for general even β > 0 does not appear to be carried out.

status_evidence.title: Painlevé Representation of Tracy–Widom_β Distribution for β = 6
status_evidence.snippet: Rumanov derives a Painlevé-II based representation of the Tracy–Widom distribution for β = 6 via a Lax-pair for the Bloemendal–Virág equation.
status_evidence.claim: Rumanov's formal Painlevé-II representation for β=6 exists in the literature.

status_evidence.title: On the Tracy-Widom β-distribution for β = 6 (Its, talk notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Rumanov's Lax-pair is interpreted as a gauge transformation of the standard Painlevé-II Lax pair; the Painlevé function involved is shown to be the Hastings–McLeod solution; integrability of the auxiliary ODE remains the key open issue.
status_evidence.claim: Partial rigorous progress for β=6 has been made, but the integrability of the auxiliary ODE remains open.
